Does a single column do what the whole model does?

Source: R/checks-validation.R
target_leakage_check.Rd

The signature of a leaked target: a field filled in after the outcome was known and joined back into the data - a settlement amount on a claims model, a closure reason on a churn model, an ID ordered by outcome. The model learns it, scores beautifully offline, and collapses in production where the column is empty at scoring time.

Usage

target_leakage_check(config = validation_config())

Arguments

config

A validation_config(); uses leakage_ratio and leakage_min_power.

Value

A gate_check.

Details

Each column's solo power is compared with the power of y_pred, on the same 0-1 scale: |2 AUC - 1| for a binary target, |r| for a continuous one, and the square root of the correlation ratio for a non-numeric column. A column is flagged (LEAKAGE_RISK, blocking) only when its power reaches both leakage_min_power and leakage_ratio times the model's: on a model scoring 0.55, a feature scoring 0.54 is 98% of it and means nothing.

Needs y_true and y_pred. The task comes from gate_context()'s task, inferred from y_true when "auto".

Port of LeakageCheck in bdp-model-gate 0.7.0, for binary and regression targets. Differences: a multiclass target is skipped with a reason (not yet ported); rows with a missing y_true are left out and counted, where upstream counts them as positives (binary) or returns OK with a model power of NaN (regression); and a model power that is not finite is skipped rather than reported.

Examples

set.seed(1)
y <- rbinom(200, 1, 0.3)
score <- plogis(-1 + 2 * y + rnorm(200))        # a reasonable model's scores
X <- data.frame(age = rnorm(200, 40, 10),
                settled_amount = y * runif(200, 1000, 5000))   # only known after the outcome
report <- run_gate(gate_context(X, y_true = y, y_pred = score), list(target_leakage_check()))
report$results[[1]]$detail
#> [1] "settled_amount alone reaches 1.000 of the target on its own, 116% of the whole model's 0.860 - check it is populated before the outcome is known, and is available at scoring time"
